citations.quote: The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. It supplies countable choice for the chosen tubular data: for any sequence of nonempty sets, apply full choice to its range and compose with the index map. Let $L=\bigcup_{i\in I}K_i$ be a finite oriented link in the standard oriented $3$-sphere, where $I$ is a finite index set. For each component $K_i$, include a chosen closed tubular neighbourhood $N(K_i)$, its exterior $E_{K_i}=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}N(K_i)$, the positive meridian $\mu_i$, and the preferred longitude $\lambda_i$; the longitude is the degree-one parallel class in $H_1(\partial E_{K_i};\mathbb Z)$ that maps to zero in $H_1(E_{K_i};\mathbb Z)$. For each $i\in I$, choose an integer $n_i$. The resulting **integral framed-link surgery diagram** is this link and integer family, with the surgery result defined by removing the interiors of all $N(K_i)$ and gluing an oriented solid torus to each boundary torus so that its meridian maps to $n_i[\mu_i]+[\lambda_i]$. If $I=\varnothing$, the surgery result is $S^3$. A diagram is considered up to orientation-preserving ambient isotopy carrying each component framing; a planar projection is only a way of drawing the link.

citations.quote: The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

Assume AC. Let $N,M$ be connected nonempty compact oriented smooth three-manifolds, with their boundaries identified with the same oriented surface $\Sigma$ in the bordism convention and with fixed compatible product collars. There is a finite framed link in $\operatorname{int}N$ whose surgery is diffeomorphic to $M$ with the prescribed external boundary parametrization. It may be realized as a four-dimensional two-handle trace with those marked horizontal faces and vertical collar $\Sigma\times[0,1]$. More generally this holds componentwise for a specified common component partition; empty input is treated by the empty union. In particular a fixed connected standard base with the required boundary may be chosen on each component, and a closed component may use $N=S^3$. An explicit connected standard base is the complement in $S^3$ of standard handlebodies placed in pairwise disjoint balls, one for each boundary component with its specified genus, with the given surface parametrizations attached to these boundary copies. This is relative surgery existence, not equivalence or completeness of surgery moves. Decorations may be carried by the resulting actual diffeomorphism; a complete decorated move theorem is a separate assertion.

For each $i\in I$, choose an integer $n_i$. The resulting **integral framed-link surgery diagram** is this link and integer family, with the surgery result defined by removing the interiors of all $N(K_i)$ and gluing an oriented solid torus to each boundary torus so that its meridian maps to $n_i[\mu_i]+[\lambda_i]$. If $I=\varnothing$, the surgery result is $S^3$. Assume the Axiom of Choice. For an integral framed link diagram, **Kirby move equivalence** is the equivalence relation generated by the following operations.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. If two integral framed-link surgery diagrams are related by one ambient isotopy, handle slide, or split $\pm1$-unknot stabilization or destabilization as defined for this page, then their oriented surgery results are orientation-preservingly diffeomorphic. The same holds for any finite sequence of these moves.

Assume full AC. Let $M:\Sigma_0\to\Sigma_1$ be any compact oriented smooth three-bordism with its fixed product collars, boundary parametrizations and a properly embedded finite colored framed ribbon graph with actual coupon morphisms and the prescribed labeled boundary ribbons. For each connected component of $M$, fix a connected standard base $N$ with exactly that parametrized external boundary: for example the complement in $S^3$ of disjoint standard handlebodies, one of the prescribed genus for each boundary component. Keep these boundary handlebodies, their attaching parametrizations and their marked cap ribbons fixed. A closed component uses $N=S^3$. Take the finite disjoint union with this specified component partition. More generally, any fixed connected compact oriented base with the same marked boundary is allowed on each component.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $L$ be a finite integral framed link in the standard oriented $S^3$. In its complement choose an oriented knot $K$ with any integer framing and a small meridian $U$ of $K$, lying in a ball about one short arc of $K$ and disjoint from $L$. Give $U$ its disk framing zero. Then $L\cup K\cup U$ and $L$ are related by a finite sequence of orientation-preserving ambient isotopies, fully framed handle slides, and insertions or deletions of split $+1$ or $-1$ framed unknots. The conclusion applies also to the inverse insertion move. No condition on the knot type of $K$ or on its linking with $L$ is imposed.
